audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Trundle five of seven stages (Trundle / Trundle / Trundle / Skill / Trundle / Skill / Trundle) in the worst lane of my slice — 47.94% over 340 games — and the whys directly beneath say the opposite for four of them: `early` opens "Levels 1-2 are genuinely his", whys[0] "do not overcommit", whys[1] "lets him win short trades before you can establish your W zone", whys[2] "the matchup is closer", whys[6] "his damage ceiling overtakes your sustain".
audit.why: Levels 1 and 2 belong to Yone and the page already argues it in prose: Mortal Steel is a 450-range linear thrust against a 300-range bite. Level 3 is even, not won. And two-plus items is his by the page's own reasoning. Only level 6 is unambiguously Trundle's, and whys[4] says so — "the one window you clearly win".
audit.corrected: Yone at levels 1, 2 and two-plus items; Skill at level 3, levels 4-5 and first item; Trundle at level 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and whys[6] describe Yone's late spike as "his E reset makes him nearly unpinnable" without a number, and `mid` gives Soul Unbound a single fixed figure: "Force trades on his E cooldown (22 seconds)".
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22/19/16/13/10 seconds. Twenty-two is only true at rank 1 — by rank 5 it is ten, which is less than half, and that halving IS his scaling in this matchup. The page states the rank-1 number as if it held all game, so a Trundle counting to twenty-two at level 13 is walking into a spirit that has already reset. Fate Sealed is also missing from the page entirely: 120/100/80 seconds, a blink behind the last champion in a line that pulls everyone it hits back toward him — the same cooldown as Subjugate.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1 falling to 10s at rank 5. Fate Sealed 120/100/80s, and it pulls.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], whys[0] and whys[1] all describe "his Q2 slow" — spikes[0] says it "makes you a sitting target". Other fields call the same cast Q3.
audit.why: There is no slow anywhere in Mortal Steel. Riot's text: at two stacks of Gathering Storm, Mortal Steel dashes Yone FORWARD with a gust of wind that knocks enemies Airborne. A knockup and a gap-close are a completely different problem from a slow — you sidestep the line rather than trying to outrun a debuff, and the empowered cast brings him to you instead of holding you in place. The page also names the same ability two ways, which makes the mistake harder to catch.
audit.corrected: Two-stack Mortal Steel is a forward dash with a knockup, not a slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields make Kraken Slayer a percent-health item: spikes[2] "percent-max-HP true damage on every third hit", whys[5], whys[6] and wants.foe[2] all build the late game on it, and `late` repeats it.
audit.why: Kraken Slayer's proc is bonus TRUE damage on a repeating attack count — it goes through resistances rather than scaling off your health bar, which is a different reason to reach the same conclusion and a different set of counters. The genuine every-other-hit mechanic in this matchup is Yone's own passive: Way of the Hunter deals magic damage with every second attack. That is never mentioned anywhere, and it is the real argument for magic resist against a champion the page treats as pure physical.
audit.corrected: Kraken Slayer: bonus true damage on a repeating attack count. Way of the Hunter: magic damage every second attack.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Cleave appears once, as "soul-cleave damage", with none of its properties. Fate Sealed appears nowhere.
audit.why: Spirit Cleave is a 700-range cone that SHIELDS him, scaling with the number of champions hit, and Riot's text says both its cooldown and its cast time scale with attack speed — so it speeds up as he itemises, and 14 seconds is a ceiling rather than a fixed number. That shield is why level-2 trades go his way. Fate Sealed matters differently: it blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him, which means standing behind your own Pillar of Ice is not the safety it looks like.
audit.corrected: Spirit Cleave (14s, 700 range) shields him and speeds up with attack speed. Fate Sealed pulls you back through your own terrain.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], wants.you[2] and whys[4] describe Subjugate only as a resistance drain, and whys[2] calls Chomp an "AS steal".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage. Subjugate takes 40% of both resistances plus 20/25/30% of the target's maximum health as damage, healing Trundle for the same amount and doubling over 4 seconds — and against a Yone who has just snapped back into his body at whatever health his spirit left him, the max-health half is what closes the window the page correctly identifies as the best one in the lane.
audit.corrected: Chomp: AD sap. Subjugate: 40% of resists plus a fifth of max health, healing the same, doubling over 4s.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Soul Unbound with no figure; the one number in the content layer, "22 seconds", is rank 1 stated as if fixed.
audit.why: Soul Unbound 22/19/16/13/10s, Spirit Cleave 14s and falling with attack speed, Mortal Steel a flat 4s, Fate Sealed 120/100/80s, against Chomp's 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s. At rank 1 Pillar of Ice and Soul Unbound trade almost exactly one for one; by rank 5 he gets two escapes per pillar, which is the honest reason this lane sours.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], spikes[3], mid, late and whys[6].

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] buys Executioner's Calling on the first back "— cuts his healing", and prescribes Plated Steelcaps against a kit that deals magic damage every second attack.
audit.why: No Yone ability carries a heal flag and _missing-interactions.json raises no needs-antiheal here; his sustain is item-borne, so the buy belongs after he has lifesteal rather than at 800 gold on the first back. Way of the Hunter's magic damage on every second attack is also a real argument for mixing in magic resist, which no field on the page makes.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling once he has lifesteal. Way of the Hunter is magic damage every second attack.

audit.why: No suspectNames were raised for this matchup. One kit-library flag note: Mortal Steel carries a dash flag which IS correct at two stacks, and Fate Sealed carries a dash flag for what Riot describes as a blink — neither changed anything I wrote.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are genuinely his — Yone's Q is a long-range linear slash you cannot trade into at level 1 without eating both hits, and his Q2 slow means chasing him back to your W is harder than it looks. Play near the wave, last-hit with Chomp when you can get in cleanly, and do not waste E Pillar trying to trap him before level 3; he will simply walk around it or E away. The one bright spot: King's Tribute heals you off every minion that dies nearby, so his poke does less than it looks like on the health bar.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are genuinely his — Mortal Steel is a 450-range linear thrust you cannot trade into without eating both hits, and at two stacks it dashes him in with a knockup, so stepping up costs more than it looks. Play near the wave, last-hit with Chomp when you can get in cleanly, and hold Pillar of Ice until 3; before that he walks around it or leaves on Soul Unbound. The one bright spot: King's Tribute heals you off every minion that dies nearby, so his poke does less than the health bar suggests.

edits.before: At level 3 the matchup becomes a timing puzzle. Your W Frozen Domain is up every time he commits a Q3 — the trick is dropping it the instant his Soul Unbound activates so that when he snaps back you are already in motion inside the speed bonus. Force trades on his E cooldown (22 seconds), not on yours. Level 6 is your clearest power window in the entire matchup: Subjugate into him mid-trade steals whatever armor and MR he has built, and if you Pillar the snap-back location correctly he cannot escape — he takes the knockup the instant he reappears. Use this window to either kill him or shove him out of lane badly enough to secure the first Rift or draw jungler pressure to your side.
edits.after: At level 3 the matchup becomes a timing puzzle. Frozen Domain is up every time he commits the two-stack Mortal Steel — drop it the instant Soul Unbound activates, so that when his spirit snaps back you are already moving inside the speed bonus. Force trades on Soul Unbound's cooldown, which is 22 seconds at rank 1 but only 10 at rank 5, so that window narrows every time he ranks it. Level 6 is your clearest spike in the matchup: Subjugate takes 40% of his armour and MR plus a fifth of his max health and heals you the same, and a Pillar of Ice on the return point leaves him nowhere to walk. Cash it into a shove, a Rift, or jungle pressure.

edits.before: Late game this lane belongs to Yone. Kraken Slayer's true damage bypasses your resistance stacking, and his E reset means a well-played Yone is genuinely difficult to pin down with Pillar alone. Your Subjugate still has enormous team-fight value against the rest of their composition — if Yone is the only target, Subjugate is wasted; look to drain their frontline tank instead. In extended side-lane duels avoid open ground where he can Q-dash through your Frozen Domain; fight only in chokepoints where the Pillar can block his E exit and force the brawl on your terms. He out-scales in the 1v1, so convert your mid-game spike into map pressure rather than trying to win the 20-minute duel.
edits.after: Late game this lane belongs to Yone. Kraken Slayer's bonus true damage on every third attack goes through resistances rather than around them, and Way of the Hunter adds magic on every second hit, so armour alone reads the duel wrong. Soul Unbound at 10 seconds by rank 5 makes him genuinely hard to pin with Pillar alone. Subjugate still has enormous team-fight value elsewhere in their composition — take their frontline tank rather than spending it on Yone. Fight in chokepoints where the Pillar seals his exit, and respect Fate Sealed: a 120-second blink behind the last champion in a line that pulls everyone it hits back to him.

notes: Chart was Trundle 5/7 over Trundle's worst win rate in this slice (47.94%), and the page's own prose already says levels 1-2 are Yone's. Fixing it required no new claims at all — only matching the labels to the paragraphs. Two ability errors worth sweeping: 'Q2 slow' (Mortal Steel's two-stack cast is a forward dash with a knockup, no slow anywhere in the ability) and Kraken Slayer as 'percent-max-HP true damage', which appears in four fields here and again in the Tryndamere entry as 'percent-current-HP'. Yone's Way of the Hunter — magic damage on every second attack — appears nowhere on the page and is the real argument for magic resist in a matchup the page itemises as pure physical.
